title: Same $200 a Month, Double the Money. The Only Difference? #shorts
description:
Two friends save the same $200 a month. Alex starts at 25, Sam at 35. At an example 7% a year, by 65 Alex has about $525,000 and Sam about $244,000, more than double, even though Alex only put in $24,000 more ($96,000 vs $72,000). That's compounding.

Math: $200 a month, 7% a year compounded monthly, contributions until age 65. 7% is an illustration, not a promise: real returns vary year to year and can be negative. Taxes, fees and inflation are not included.

This video is for education only and is not financial advice.
